text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are concerned about your infant's bilious vomiting, inability to pass meconium, and abdominal distension. Have they passed any stool or gas since birth, and how old is the baby exactly?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-day-old male infant. The infant was born via a home birth without complications. The mother reports that the infant has had bilious vomiting and has not been able to pass meconium since birth. She also notes that the infant's abdomen appears distended.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung Disease (Congenital Aganglionic Megacolon).

The combination of bilious vomiting, failure to pass meconium, and abdominal distension in a 2-day-old infant is highly suggestive of this condition. I am requesting an abdominal X-ray and a contrast enema to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray; REQUEST IMAGES: Contrast_Enema.
